operator.name: hereditary final-mover cap closure
operator.rule: delete from player 1-f every residual containing every currently open top cap

proof_candidate: occupying every current open top cap fills every currently nonfull column and therefore fills the board
the last such occupation is the final board move and belongs to f
player 1-f therefore cannot complete a residual containing every current cap
a surviving descendant of such a residual continues to contain every new open cap, so deadness is hereditary
G-deleted residuals cannot create a terminal token
strict supersets hidden by antichain normalization are dead for the same reason
G is column-permutation covariant because the open-cap set transports bijectively and f is unchanged

exact_finite.statement: On complete 4x4, G alone is a literal Q-F transition congruence with 31,794 classes, and all tested R/F/G compositions are Q-F/QA/QV exact.
On complete 4x4, RFG is the smallest tested direct Q-F representation with 30,046 classes.
On complete 4x4, Sigma(RFG) is the smallest tested transporter-aware Q-F representation with 9,308 classes.
The new 9,308-class Q-F candidate is strictly smaller than the prior 9,508-class Q-A/Q-V candidate based on the turn-restricted final-cap rule C.
Complete 3x3-k3, 3x4-k3, 4x3-k3 and 4x4-k4 controls all independently verify G and RFG transition factorization, G idempotence, RG/FG commutation, column covariance and transported factorization.

interpretation: The earlier Q-F versus Q-A/Q-V gap was not fundamental in the tested carrier; it exposed that C was a non-hereditary slice of a stronger rank-local dead-information rule.
The new G operator is a direct current-rank structural recognizer, not a carried history bit.
The current leading tested Q-F/Q-A/Q-V representation is q_SigmaRFG.
